description: part2 v0: Part 1 champion spec refit natively on emerging (no changes)
part2 bar: developed base alone (Part 1 spec fit on developed 2021-23), level balanced on train, level-neutral metric, folds B+R

E1 region credibility factor — the base has never seen E01-E06 and diagnostics.md flags region E04 PERSISTENT on contents (A/E 1.17 B / 1.91 R, 4.2% exposure), and region is the top untried Tier 0 backlog item.

P0 — sum of the fine per-peril developed bases at level 1 (no emerging-fitted shrinkage) vs. the single total-cost base, since for buildings/contents (and motor's fine-split "other" perils) each `base_<peril>` is its own independent refit, not an algebraic share of `base`.

P1 — peril_levels(k=100) per line on top of kept P0, letting each peril's emerging/base cost ratio move (credibility-shrunk by claim count towards the line's overall ratio) instead of freezing every level at 1.0.

Re-test backlog E1 (region credibility factor) — the first attempt (2026-10-25T01:45:52, discard 0.13515) used raw y/base per region level, baking the developed-to-emerging level gap into the factor instead of isolating the relativity; `credibility_factors()` already normalises A/E to the line's own A/E before shrinking, so this retry applies it correctly, and the backlog explicitly says to re-test it first before moving on.

Backlog P2 — peril_levels(k=100) on motor only, since P1's loss (0.13820 < kept P0 0.13778) came from letting every peril move, including buildings fire which the backlog flags as noisy; motor glass/hail is the one clearly shifted peril (O6: 1.6-1.8x developed frequency).

Backlog P3 — peril_levels(k=30) on motor only, retrying the better of P1 (every line, 0.13820) / P2 (motor only, 0.13823) at less shrinkage, since both already nudged the primary above kept P0 (0.13778) but under the 0.001 keep margin.

backlog P4 — geometric blend (w=0.5) of `base` and the P2 motor-level peril-sum, since the two fold winners split (bar wins fold B, kept P0 wins fold R) and P1-P3's k sweep on motor peril levels is already near its shrinkage floor (z>0.9), so no more k values are worth testing.

E3 — joint ridge log-link Tweedie GLM correction (region, age band, new_business, channel, +cover_type on motor) on top of the kept P0 peril-sum base, alpha=10, since marginal credibility factors on region (E1) and age band (owner check) both lost on both folds, plausibly because region and new_business are confounded on a 76%-new-business broker book and a joint fit can net that out where univariate factors can't.

Backlog E4 — hail_days/wildfire_index sit far outside the developed training range (part2_drift.md PSI 1.8-6.5, motor glass_hail frequency 1.55-1.84x developed), so the base's trees extrapolate flat there; untried while E1/E3 discarded and E2 owner-ruled-out.

backlog E5 (renewal_count capped at 3) — untried; the owner's manual check only tested new_business by count (+0.0003, noise), and reports/part2_drift.md shows renewal_count/customer_tenure PSI from emg_train to the 2025 test rows is 2.0-2.1 on every line, the largest train/test shift in the drift table, since 76% of 2025 is new business.

backlog E6 — sum insured credibility factor on buildings/contents, since contents sum insured averages 113k vs 125k developed and 2025 buildings sum insured is 731k vs 680k in training (reports/part2_drift.md), a size-of-risk shift the base's banded relativity may not carry correctly; next untried Tier 0 item (E1/E3/E4/E5 all tried and discarded).

E7 — a tiny whitelisted LightGBM correction (region, age band, hail_days, wildfire_index, new_business) on top of kept P0, since every Tier 0 univariate credibility factor lost on both folds but can't net out confounding the way a joint model can.

E10 — per-line switch, peril-sum only on motor (where it helped fold B in kept P0) and plain `base` on buildings/contents (where the per-peril refits added estimation noise), since no per-line R split exists in the ledger to know which line carried P0's R gain.

E8 (backlog Tier 1) — an EBM correction on the same five-field whitelist that broke LightGBM (E7, discard 0.12431) should avoid that failure mode because it is additive with zero interactions and coarsely binned, so it can't carve out the noisy category combinations a multi-way tree split can.

backlog Tier 2 E11 — geometric blend of the kept P0 peril-sum base with `native` (iaa.experiment.fit_predict refit directly on emerging train data), since every Tier 0/1 structured correction (E1-E10) lost on both folds but a small dose of the native fit's ranking signal, heavily shrunk, hasn't been tried.

Stack the ledger's two best-performing corrections multiplicatively (backlog E12) — P3's motor peril_levels(k=30) and E5's renewal_count-capped-at-3 count-basis credibility factor — since both individually landed closest to beating kept P0 and act on orthogonal fields (motor glass/hail mix vs. tenure shift across all lines).

credibility factor on motor `fuel_type` (diesel 29.5% exposure, A/E 1.13 fold B / 1.11 fold R, PERSISTENT in diagnostics.md) on top of kept P0, since no Tier 0 factor tried so far targeted a large persistent diagnostic miss — E1/E5/E6 all hit fields the diagnostics table doesn't flag PERSISTENT.

Combine E3's joint GLM (region/age_band/new_business/channel/cover_type) with E4's weather signal as standardised numerics in the same model, since both individually came within ~0.001–0.0012 of beating kept P0 and backlog E4 explicitly suggests this fold-in, which hasn't been tried.

Stack the motor-only fuel_type credibility factor (03:21:06, discard 0.13877, short of the keep margin by 0.00001) onto the kept E12 pair (03:16:40, discard 0.13852: P3's motor peril_levels k=30 × E5's renewal_count-capped-at-3 factor), since the three act on orthogonal fields and the ledger shows the first two stacked additively.

Backlog P3's second named value, k=300 (more shrinkage) for motor peril_levels, is untried — only k=30 was tested (2026-10-25T02:39:25, discard 0.13830) and then carried into the kept champion stacked with E5's renewal factor and the fuel factor.

Stack a motor `cover_type` cost-basis credibility factor (k=200) onto the kept champion (E12 peril-levels+renewal+fuel, primary 0.13948), since diagnostics against that champion flags third_party_fire_theft (10.7% exposure) PERSISTENT with a wider both-fold A/E gap (0.857 B / 0.874 R) than the fuel_type miss that already passed, and cover_type has only three levels so little overfit risk, unlike region/occupation which lost.

motor-only elevation_m quintile credibility factor (cost basis, k=200, fuel_type's exact recipe) — diagnostics.md against the current champion flags elevation_m PERSISTENT at both tails (15.3-60: A/E 0.83 B/0.80 R, 19.9% exposure; 0-3: 1.19 B/1.10 R, 20.0% exposure), the largest residual motor miss by exposure×gap after fuel_type, since region E01-E06's developed-terrain relativity transfers imperfectly.

Stack both near-miss motor factors (cover_type k=200, elevation_m quintile k=200) onto the kept champion at once, since each alone raised both folds but fell short of the 0.001 keep margin (cover_type +0.00027 on 2026-10-25T03:35:36; elevation_m +0.00088 on 2026-10-25T03:40:44) and stacking has been near-additive all day.

energy_rating credibility factor on buildings and contents, since diagnostics.md flags it PERSISTENT with a large gap on buildings (level E, 10.0% exposure, A/E 1.509 B/1.839 R) and simultaneously on three contents levels (A/B/C, 14.5-17.4% exposure each) — the same field mis-ranking two lines in the same direction, and untried in the ledger.

backlog E6 (sum insured credibility factor) — untried while every other Tier 0 field has been tried or owner-ruled-out, and part2_drift.md shows a property-size shift in both directions (contents 113k emerging vs 125k developed; buildings 731k vs 680k).

credibility factor on previous_insurer (all three lines, k=200) stacked onto the kept champion — diagnostics flags it PERSISTENT on motor (5 levels) and buildings (3 levels), it's admissible and untried as a structured factor, and the drift report shows it's one of the strongest real adversarial signals on every line's core field set

Stack the two near-miss discards from this session — energy_rating (buildings+contents, 2026-10-25T03:47:04, +0.00071 both folds) and previous_insurer (2026-10-25T03:51:40, +0.00066 both folds, restricted here to motor+buildings since contents' own component D² fell in that run) — onto the kept champion, since each alone cleared both folds but missed the 0.001 margin, and today's two keeps (fuel-on-E12, cover+elevation) came from exactly this pattern.

construction_type credibility factor on buildings — diagnostics.md's PERSISTENT list against the current kept champion (e9e329e, 0.14061) flags non_standard construction (10.2% exposure, A/E 1.464 B / 1.380 R, both folds the same direction) as the largest untouched buildings miss, and it's an admissible, actuarially standard rating field no prior run has tried.

missed_payments_12m credibility factor on motor+buildings — untried in the ledger, and diagnostics.md flags it PERSISTENT with large both-fold A/E gaps on both lines (motor 6.2% exp, 1.232 B/1.178 R; buildings 6.3% exp, 1.347 B/2.065 R, the biggest gap in the buildings table).

buildings `years_at_address` credibility factor (k=200, cost basis) — diagnostics.md flags two PERSISTENT bands moving opposite ways on both folds (0-3yr under-predicted 1.248B/1.280R, 7-10yr over-predicted 0.720B/0.702R, 35% combined exposure), untried in the ledger.

retest missed_payments_12m (motor+buildings, 2026-10-25T04:01:17, discard 0.14279, +0.00075 both folds but under the 0.001 margin) on a residual basis — the factor's A/E is now measured against the champion's own stacked prediction (mirrored onto training rows as `out_tr`) instead of raw `base`, since the old raw-basis estimate likely double-counted its overlap with the already-applied `renewal_count` factor (new business lacks 12-month payment history).

pair the confirmed near-miss missed_payments_12m (motor+buildings, raw basis, discard 0.14279 at 04:01, +0.00075 both folds) with a fresh diagnostics-driven candidate, trees_within_5m on buildings (11.7% exposure, A/E 1.316 B/1.641 R, untouched), the same two-near-miss stacking pattern that produced today's three keeps.

contents `works_from_home` credibility factor (k=200, cost basis) on top of the kept champion (27c76eb, 0.14342) — PERSISTENT at 25.0% exposure, the largest untried admissible field by exposure share, binary so low overfit risk, orthogonal to contents' existing renewal_count/energy_rating factors.

pair the confirmed near-miss works_from_home (contents, discard 0.14378 at 04:15:49, +0.00036 both folds vs. kept champion 0.14342) with a fresh diagnostics-driven candidate, years_licensed on motor (20.3% exposure, A/E 0.878 B/0.840 R, the largest untouched PERSISTENT motor miss, untried), the same two-near-miss stacking pattern that produced today's four keeps.

pair the confirmed near-miss works_from_home (contents, 2026-10-25T04:15:49, discard 0.14378, +0.00036 both folds alone) with a fresh diagnostics-driven candidate, contents voluntary_excess (29.8% exposure, the largest untried PERSISTENT contents miss, A/E 1.153 B / 1.258 R), the same two-near-miss stacking pattern that produced today's three keeps — the last pairing attempt failed because years_licensed was the wrong partner, not because pairing itself stopped working.

pair the confirmed near-miss contents `works_from_home` factor (discard 0.14378 alone on the current champion, +0.00036 both folds) with a fresh diagnostics-driven candidate on the same line, `high_value_items` (PERSISTENT at two contents levels moving opposite ways: 4.0 at 4.2% exposure A/E 0.561B/0.667R, 2.0 at 10.3% exposure A/E 1.219B/1.211R), since backing out the marginals of the two prior failed pairings (years_licensed, voluntary_excess) shows those partners were themselves net-negative, not that pairing fails.

Pair the confirmed near-miss contents `works_from_home` factor (discard 0.14378, +0.00036 both folds alone) with a fresh multi-line diagnostic signal, `occupation` (PERSISTENT on all three lines in diagnostics.md, untried as a structured factor), since the last three pairing attempts used small single-line partners that netted almost nothing.

household_size is PERSISTENT on all three lines in diagnostics.md against the current champion (motor 8.2%, buildings 14.0%, contents 14.1%, all under-predicting actual in the same direction), the same multi-line signature that made occupation (v7) a kept winner, and it's untried and fully admissible.

buildings `flood_zone` credibility factor — PERSISTENT in diagnostics.md with the largest unaddressed exposure×gap on buildings (band 3.0, 7.6% exposure, A/E 1.276B/1.605R under-predicted; band 2.0, 14.6% exposure, A/E 0.770B/0.695R over-predicted), untried as a structured factor, and the last single-field attempt (household_size, discard 0.14382) was a clean loss with no near-miss to pair.

pair the confirmed near-miss `flood_zone` on buildings (discard 2026-10-25T04:31:55, +0.00038 both folds, just under the 0.001 keep margin) with `marital_status` on all three lines, PERSISTENT in diagnostics.md against the current champion (motor married 39.3% exposure, buildings divorced 7.3%, contents missing 12.0%) and untried — the same multi-line pattern that made occupation (v7) a keep.

Pair the confirmed near-miss buildings `flood_zone` factor (discard 0.14497, +0.00038 both folds alone) with a fresh diagnostics-driven candidate, `basement` on buildings (PERSISTENT, 14.5% exposure, A/E 0.746 B / 0.675 R, both folds over-predicted ~27-33%), since the only prior pairing attempt used `marital_status` which was net negative, not evidence that pairing fails.

region credibility factor on buildings only (k=200) — diagnostics flags buildings region E06 PERSISTENT at 19.9% exposure, the largest untried buildings field; prior region attempts (backlog E1) applied it across all lines against a much weaker champion, likely diluted by noisier motor/contents region levels.

soil_type credibility factor on motor+contents — PERSISTENT against the current champion (6da0d19, 0.14459) on both lines at once (motor loam 13.9% exposure, contents clay/missing 31.2%+12.3%), the same multi-line signature that made occupation a kept winner, and untried as a structured factor.

stack the two orthogonal confirmed near-misses left open against the current champion (6da0d19, 0.14459) — buildings flood_zone+basement (discard 0.14514, +0.00055 both folds) and motor+contents soil_type (discard 0.14475, +0.00016 both folds) — since they touch disjoint lines/fields and today's prior near-miss stacks combined near-additively or better.

licence_points credibility factor on motor alone — the one remaining PERSISTENT diagnostic field with a clear actuarial mechanism (driving-behaviour points, enforcement differs by market), untried, 12.1% exposure, A/E 1.121 B / 1.239 R, admissible (owner's ban is property-only).

extend the existing energy_rating credibility factor from buildings+contents to all three lines, since diagnostics.md flags it PERSISTENT on motor too (level A, 14.0% exposure, A/E 0.891B/0.927R, same under-predicted direction) and it's an address attribute, not a vehicle one, so it's untried on motor.

pair the confirmed near-miss buildings `flood_zone` factor (discard 2026-10-25T04:31:55, +0.00038 both folds alone) with a fresh diagnostics-driven candidate, contents `security_level` (PERSISTENT "missing" level, 12.1% exposure, A/E 0.824 B / 0.632 R), since both are untried in this combination and orthogonal (buildings vs. contents).

contents `voluntary_excess` credibility factor (basis=count, k=200) — the largest untried PERSISTENT contents miss against the current champion (29.8% exposure, A/E 1.155 B / 1.258 R), with a clear frequency-selection mechanism (higher voluntary excess self-selects lower claim frequency).

pair the confirmed near-miss buildings `flood_zone` factor (+0.00038 alone vs. current champion, 2026-10-25T04:31:55) with a fresh, untried, larger diagnostic signal on a different line, contents `document_preference` (14.8% exposure, A/E 0.753B/0.713R, both folds), since flood_zone's small-field buildings pairings (marital_status, basement, soil_type, security_level) all topped out at +0.00072.

pair the open confirmed near-miss buildings `flood_zone` factor (2026-10-25T04:31:55, discard 0.14497, +0.00038 both folds alone) with a fresh diagnostics-driven candidate, buildings `policyholder_age_band` — untried, and the largest gap in the whole diagnostics table (16.2% exposure, A/E 0.710 fold B / 0.318 fold R).

pair the open confirmed near-miss buildings `flood_zone` factor (discard 2026-10-25T04:31:55, +0.00038 both folds alone) with motor `mean_temperature_c`, PERSISTENT in diagnostics.md against this champion (19.9% exposure, A/E 0.875 B / 0.922 R) and the only sizeable untried motor field left, following the pairing pattern that produced this session's three keeps.
owner re-base (25 Oct midday): P0 per-peril developed base, gender admissible, deploy metric frozen (folds B+R, 2:1 natural:test-mix weighted, margin 0.002, bootstrap q10>0, ln guard). Board 0.15195

L1 motor gender, offset_glm on P0 (offset `p0`) with cols ["gender"], alpha=0.01 (setting 2 of 3), gated with `lr_gate(n_tests=1)` — gate evidence in the backlog already shows motor gender passes in both years, and diagnostics.md shows the current champion still misprices gender on motor (M A/E 1.168 B / 1.119 R, F 0.831 B / 0.883 R, PERSISTENT), which P0 can't capture since the developed base has no gender field.

L2 (motor gender x driver_age_band), alpha=0.01 — the best-of-L1 setting, since L1's gender-only factor (alpha=0.01) was kept at 2026-10-25T11:16:18; L2 is the pre-registered next tier-L item and tests whether adding driver_age_band mains plus the (gender, driver_age_band) interaction, gated as one block, beats L1's gender-only correction on motor.

L2 motor gender x driver_age_band, alpha=0.1 (10x the best-of-L1 setting), the second and last pre-registered alpha for this mechanism — alpha=0.01 already discarded (2026-10-25T11:18:27), and the discard reverted all the way to plain P0 rather than falling back to L1's kept gender-only factor, since the gender+age-band+interaction block is gated as a single unit; a heavier ridge penalty may let the block pass the gate (or shrink the interaction hard enough to recover most of L1's gain) without the age-band/interaction noise that likely sank alpha=0.01.

SMOKE CRASH (smoke fold B: ok (37500 train rows, 37500 valid rows)): backlog tier L3 (motor joint GLM), alpha=0.01 — gate each of the 8 candidate columns (gender, driver_age_band, new_business, region, cover_type, occupation, vehicle_value_group, ncb_years) against p0 with n_tests=8, then fit one ridge GLM on whichever pass.

SMOKE CRASH (smoke fold B: ok (37500 train rows, 37500 valid rows)): backlog tier L3 (motor joint GLM), alpha=0.01 — gate each of the 8 candidate columns (gender, driver_age_band, new_business, region, cover_type, occupation, vehicle_value_group, ncb_years) against p0 with n_tests=8, then fit one ridge GLM on whichever pass. Setting 1 of 3; the prior attempt at this same setting (11:21:12) crashed before producing a score, so it is being run for the first time.

backlog tier L3 (motor joint GLM), alpha=0.01 (setting 1 of 3) — gate each of the 8 candidate columns (gender, driver_age_band, new_business, region, cover_type, occupation, vehicle_value_group, ncb_years) against p0 with n_tests=8, then fit one ridge GLM on whichever pass.

L3 motor joint GLM, alpha=0.1 (setting 2 of 3), because alpha=0.01 (setting 1, run 11:29:52) discarded badly — primary 0.11048, below even the bar — likely from several gated categoricals (occupation at 20 levels, region, vehicle_value_group) sharing one weakly-penalised ridge; the remaining untried settings are 0.001 (weaker shrinkage, would overfit harder) and 0.1 (stronger), so 0.1 is the one worth testing next.

L3 motor joint GLM, alpha=0.001 (setting 3 of 3) — the last pre-registered setting for this mechanism; alpha=0.01 and 0.1 both lost to the kept L1 gender-only champion (primaries 0.11048 and 0.11610 vs 0.11910), so this closes out L3 before moving to L4.

Backlog L4 (property joint GLMs), alpha=0.01 (setting 1 of 3) — L1 (motor gender) is kept, L2 and L3 both discarded at every setting, so L4 is next in tier order; buildings (gender, policyholder_age_band, new_business, region, construction_type, energy_rating) and contents (gender, policyholder_age_band, new_business, region, tenure, works_from_home) each get a pre-registered candidate list, every candidate gated individually against p0 (n_tests=6 per line), and only the ones that pass enter one ridge GLM per line on top of P0, alongside the kept L1 motor factor.

Backlog L4 (property joint GLMs), alpha=0.1 (setting 2 of 3) — setting 1 (alpha=0.01) discarded with primary 0.11278, below the L1 bar of 0.11910, so trying the next pre-registered, stronger ridge penalty on the same gated candidate lists before retiring the mechanism.

Backlog L4 (property joint GLMs), alpha=1 (setting 3 of 3) — settings 1 (0.01) and 2 (0.1) both discarded below the L1 bar, so this closes out the mechanism with the strongest pre-registered ridge penalty.

L5 (backlog tier L), motor new_business × driver_age_band interaction, alpha=0.01 (setting 1 of 2) — testing whether the 2025 emerging book's younger, 76%-new-business mix means motor new-business status interacts with age band on top of P0, since L1 (gender) is kept but L2/L3's richer motor blocks all failed the gate, and this is the next untried pre-registered motor mechanism.
backlog L5 (motor new_business x driver_age_band on top of P0), alpha=0.1 (setting 2 of 2) — closing out the mechanism after alpha=0.01 failed the gate.
L6, per-peril emerging levels (`peril_levels`), k=100 (setting 1 of 2), applied on every line on top of P0, stacked with the kept L1 motor gender factor.

L6 per-peril emerging levels, k=300 (setting 2 of 2) — k=100 discarded (primary 0.12007, +0.00097 over the L1 bar, under the 0.002 margin), so this closes out the mechanism with the heavier pre-registered shrinkage, stacked under the kept L1 motor gender factor.
